items.title: W.T. "Ed" Kirkeby Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: when Reds and Red Nickel and our trombone, Tommy Dorsey joined, why we put them in

ctx.x: Well, you know, we, when Nichols, Jimmy Dorsey, and Tommy Dorsey joined the Ramblers, we had a group called the Little Ramblers, of which I had Bill Moore, known as Jazz Moore, on trumpet. And we had Adrian Rillenny, of course, on bass. We used no trombone. Stan King was on drums. We had Jimmy Dorsey on saxophone. That was the first Little Ramblers. And, of course, when Reds and Red Nickel and our trombone, Tommy Dorsey joined, why we put them in, and, of course, we really began to get some real sound.
This is, in a sense, a big step in sophistication after the jazz band, New Orleans jazz band, wasn't it?

items.title: W.T. "Ed" Kirkeby Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I made records for them under Ananda Plume by the original Ramblers, with Red Nichols and Jimmy Dorsey and Tommy Dorsey

ctx.x: 1140 Broadway. In fact, I auditioned the original California Ramblers down at 1140 Broadway in the Paramount. And, of course, I made records for them under Ananda Plume by the original Ramblers, with Red Nichols and Jimmy Dorsey and Tommy Dorsey, and, of course, Adrian Rilline, who developed into the greatest bass saxophone player in the world. So we had a real team at that time, you know, with great stars. And, as I say, I think I used about 20 nom de plumes or more. And I think that, as far as recording is…
Well, I think more than any other man also, you've confused the picture for the jazz historian who tries to follow all the places you've been.
